name: Use an abacus
blurb: The soroban is fast, and skilled users beat calculators for addition. It also builds a spatial mental-arithmetic ability that persists after you put the beads away.
gear: A Japanese soroban (one bead above, four below)
steps: Learn the layout and how to represent numbers: each lower bead is one, each upper bead is five, columns are place values.
Learn the correct finger technique — thumb up, index down — which matters for speed.
Learn simple addition and subtraction within a single column.
Learn the complements: the five and ten friend rules that handle carrying and borrowing. This is the real content of the method.
Drill columns of numbers daily for speed and accuracy.
Learn anzan: visualising the beads and calculating mentally without the device, which is where the real benefit lies.
tips: Learn the finger technique properly from the start. Bad habits cap your speed permanently.
Daily short practice beats occasional long sessions for this kind of motor-plus-mental skill.
proof: You add a column of twenty three-digit numbers faster and more accurately than by pen and paper.
